en.title: Main sights of the capital
en.summary: The best-known places to visit in London and how to plan a day.

paragraphs: London has too many sights to see in one visit. This lesson teaches you to suggest, choose and plan, using shall we and let's.

Most visitors see Buckingham Palace, the home of the monarch in London, Westminster Abbey and the Houses of Parliament. Big Ben is the nickname of the great bell in the clock tower. The British Museum and the National Gallery are free to enter, and the London Eye is a giant wheel beside the Thames. Two tourists plan their day.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: Buckingham Palace, then Westminster Abbey and Big Ben.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: Yes, entry is free, although special exhibitions cost money.

lines.speaker: Hugo
lines.text: Shall we go there after lunch?

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: Good idea. Let's take the Underground, and then we can walk along the river.

lines.speaker: Hugo
lines.text: And in the evening, we could go on the London Eye.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: Let's book tickets in advance, so we don't have to queue.

paragraphs: **1. Shall we and let's suggest an activity.** Shall we... ? asks for agreement; Let's proposes a plan. See Introduction to Grammar: Moods, command, subjunctive and conditional.

blocks.html:
FormExample
What shall we + verb?What shall we see first?
Let's + verbLet's take the Underground.
We could + verbWe could go on the London Eye.
Why don't we + verb?Why don't we walk along the river?

paragraphs: **2. Free, costs and entry.** Use free for no cost and cost as a verb. See Introduction to Grammar: Adjectives.

blocks.html:
PhraseExample
is freeEntry is free.
costs moneySpecial exhibitions cost money.
free of chargeAdmission is free of charge.
book in advanceBook in advance to avoid queues.

items: Big Ben is the nickname of the great bell in the clock tower at Westminster.
The London Eye is a giant wheel beside the Thames.
Exhibition means a public display of objects.

paragraphs: Many national museums in London are free to enter, though they welcome donations. The Changing of the Guard at Buckingham Palace takes place at 11 am on certain days, and it attracts large crowds.
